text: 1789. Paris is starving.
The queen says: let them eat cake.
Except... she never said it.
Marie Antoinette: the cake myth.
The line comes from a book by Rousseau.
He wrote that around 1765.
About "a great princess." No name.
In 1765, Marie Antoinette was nine.
And living in Austria.
Also, he wrote brioche. Not cake.
Wrong age. Wrong country. Wrong pastry.
During a bread riot, she wrote they must help the people.
But the revolution needed a villain.
Nasty pamphlets made her the bad guy.
The quote got pinned on her, and it stuck.
Today it's on mugs and t-shirts.
Who really said it? Nobody knows.
Cakes offered by Marie Antoinette: zero.
History: complicated. The quote: fake.
Anyway, here's the queen with her cake.
